title: "Yeast MIG1 deletion: differential expression"
output: html_document

# Section 1: Setup
```{r setup}
pkgs <- c("DESeq2", "rtracklayer", "ggplot2", "pheatmap", "RColorBrewer",
          "EnhancedVolcano", "org.Sc.sgd.db", "clusterProfiler", "enrichplot", "apeglm")

# Load each package and remember the ones that are not available
missing <- character()
for (p in pkgs) {
  ok <- suppressWarnings(suppressPackageStartupMessages(
    require(p, character.only = TRUE, quietly = TRUE)))
  if (!ok) missing <- c(missing, p)
}

# Report
if (length(missing) > 0) {
  cat("NOT available:", paste(missing, collapse = ", "), "\n")
} else {
  cat("All packages loaded.\n")
}

# Versions of the packages that loaded
print(sapply(setdiff(pkgs, missing), function(p) as.character(packageVersion(p))))
```

# Section 2 : Settings
```{r settings}
counts_file <- "results/counts/count_matrix.tsv"
meta_file   <- "metadata/samples.tsv"
padj_cutoff <- 0.05
lfc_cutoff  <- 1
min_count   <- 10
```


# Section 3: Load data
Read the counts and the sample sheet, put the samples in the same order, and check.
```{r load_data}
#1 Read the two tables: counts and metadata
counts <- read.delim(counts_file, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
meta <- read.delim(meta_file)

dim(counts)  # shows dimensions of the counts table
dim(meta)
names(meta) # shows the column names of the metadata table  

colnames(counts) # shows the column names of the counts table
meta$run_accession  # shows the run_accession column of the metadata table

meta <- meta[match(colnames(counts), meta$run_accession), ] # Reorder the metadata table to match the order of the counts table

rownames(meta) <- meta$run_accession  # Set the row names of the metadata table to be the run_accession values

stopifnot(identical(rownames(meta), colnames(counts))) # Check that the row names of the metadata table match the column names of the counts table

meta
table(meta$condition)  # shows the number of samples in each condition

```

# Section 4: DESeq2 - Build the DESeq2 object
```{r Build dds}

meta$condition <- factor(meta$condition, levels = c("WT", "KO"))  
# Set the order of the levels for the condition factor, with "WT" as the reference level
# The order of the levels matters because DESeq2 will use the first level as the reference for comparisons. 
# In this case, "WT" is the reference, and "KO" will be compared against it.

dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = as.matrix(counts),
                              colData = meta,
                              design = ~ condition)
# this creates a DESeqDataSet object from the count matrix and the metadata, specifying that we want to model the counts based on the condition (WT vs KO).

dds
colData(dds)
levels(dds$condition)
design(dds)

```

# Section 5: Filter low-count genes

Genes with almost no reads cannot be tested reliably. They add noise and count in the multiple-testing correction, so they are removed before the model is fitted.

```{r Filter low-count genes}
keep <- rowSums(counts(dds)) >= min_count  # This creates a logical vector indicating which genes have a total count of at least min_count across all samples. Genes with fewer counts than this threshold will be filtered out.
cat("Genes before filtering:", nrow(dds), "\n")
dds <- dds[keep, ]  # Subset the DESeqDataSet to keep only the genes that have a total count of at least min_count across all samples
cat("Genes after filtering: ", nrow(dds), "\n")

# Comparing another rule

n_min <- min(table(dds$condition))                       # smallest group size = 2

# Compare the two rules before choosing
keep_A <- rowSums(counts(dds)) >= min_count              # total count >= 10
keep_B <- rowSums(counts(dds) >= min_count) >= n_min     # >= 10 reads in at least 2 samples
table(RuleA = keep_A, RuleB = keep_B)

# Apply Rule B
cat("Genes before filtering:", nrow(dds), "\n")
dds <- dds[keep_B, ]
cat("Genes after filtering: ", nrow(dds), "\n")

```

# Section 6: Run the DESeq2 model

```{r Run DESeq2 model}
dds <- DESeq(dds)

sizeFactors(dds)  # shows the size factors for each sample, which are used to normalize the counts
head(dispersions(dds))  # shows the estimated dispersion values for each gene, which are used to model the variability in the counts
resultsNames(dds)  # shows the names of the coefficients in the model, which can be used to extract specific results
```


# Section 7: Results

```{r Results}
res <- results(dds, contrast = c("condition", "KO", "WT"), alpha = padj_cutoff)

summary(res)
head(res[order(res$padj), ])      # the most significant genes
res["YGL035C", ]                  # MIG1, your positive control

```


# Section 8: Shrink the fold changes

```{r Shrink fold changes}
res_shrunk <- lfcShrink(dds, coef = "condition_KO_vs_WT", type = "apeglm", res = res)

# Compare shrunken with unshrunken, for MIG1 and for a few low-count genes
comparison <- data.frame(baseMean = res$baseMean,
                         lfc_mle  = res$log2FoldChange,
                         lfc_shrunk = res_shrunk$log2FoldChange,
                         row.names = rownames(res))
comparison["YGL035C", ]
head(comparison[order(comparison$baseMean), ])     # the lowest-count genes
plot(comparison$lfc_mle, comparison$lfc_shrunk, pch = 16, cex = 0.4)
abline(0, 1, col = "red")                          # the line where shrunken = unshrunken

```


# Section 9: Diagnostic plots

```{r Diagnostic plots}

plotDispEsts(dds)

# seeing the outliers
outliers <- rownames(dds)[mcols(dds)$dispOutlier]
length(outliers)
head(outliers, 20)

plotMA(res_shrunk, ylim = c(-5, 5))

hist(res$pvalue[res$baseMean > 1], breaks = 20, col = "grey70",
     main = "p-value histogram", xlab = "p-value")

```

# Section 10: Annotate the results

```{r Annotate results}
gtf_file <- "data/reference/annotation.gtf"

gtf <- rtracklayer::import(gtf_file)
genes_df <- as.data.frame(gtf[gtf$type == "gene"])
colnames(genes_df)
head(genes_df[, c("gene_id", "gene_name")])
sum(is.na(genes_df$gene_name))  # how many genes have no gene_name


# Annotate the results, apply the cutoffs and save

out_dir <- "results/deseq2"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# 1. Lookup table: one row per gene, with a label (name if it exists, otherwise the ID)
gene_info <- genes_df[, c("gene_id", "gene_name", "gene_biotype")]
gene_info$label <- ifelse(is.na(gene_info$gene_name), gene_info$gene_id, gene_info$gene_name)

#2 One result table with both fold changes (shrunken and unshrunken)
res_table <- data.frame(gene_id = rownames(res),
                        baseMean = res$baseMean,
                        log2FC_mle = res$log2FoldChange,
                        log2FC_shrunk = res_shrunk$log2FoldChange,
                        lfcSE = res_shrunk$lfcSE,
                        pvalue = res_shrunk$pvalue,
                        padj = res_shrunk$padj)
res_table <- merge(res_table, gene_info, by = "gene_id", all.x = TRUE)
stopifnot(nrow(res_table) == nrow(res))  # check that the merge didn't change the number of rows

#3 Apply the cutoffs
sig <- !is.na(res_table$padj) & res_table$padj < padj_cutoff &
       abs(res_table$log2FC_shrunk) > lfc_cutoff
res_table$direction <- ifelse(sig & res_table$log2FC_shrunk > 0, "up in KO",
                       ifelse(sig & res_table$log2FC_shrunk < 0, "down in KO", "not significant"))
table(res_table$direction)

# 4. Sort by significance and save
res_table <- res_table[order(res_table$padj), ]
write.csv(res_table, file.path(out_dir, "deseq2_results_annotated.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(as.data.frame(counts(dds, normalized = TRUE)), file.path(out_dir, "normalized_counts.csv"))

head(res_table[, c("gene_id", "label", "log2FC_shrunk", "padj", "direction")], 10)
res_table[res_table$gene_id == "YGL035C", ]
```

# section 10a : More information: look beyond the top 10

```{r More information}
sig_table <- res_table[res_table$direction != "not significant", ]
cols <- c("gene_id", "label", "baseMean", "log2FC_shrunk", "padj")

head(sig_table[order(-sig_table$log2FC_shrunk), cols], 15)   # biggest increases in KO
head(sig_table[order(sig_table$log2FC_shrunk), cols], 15)    # biggest decreases in KO
table(sig_table$gene_biotype)                                # what kinds of genes?

# Known MIG1 targets (glucose-repressed genes) as a biological check
known <- c("MIG1", "SUC2", "GAL1", "GAL10", "GAL7", "GAL2", "HXT2")
res_table[res_table$label %in% known, c(cols, "direction")]

# Since sample 784 is the odd one out, check that the top genes change in both KO samples and not just one
top_ids <- head(res_table$gene_id, 10)
round(counts(dds, normalized = TRUE)[top_ids, ])

# An extension to the check, for all 389 significant genes. 
# With 2 samples per group, the strictest consistency test is “both KO samples are above both WT samples” (or below, for down genes). 
# This measures how many of your genes pass it:

norm <- counts(dds, normalized = TRUE)
wt <- c("SRR6108775", "SRR6108776")
ko <- c("SRR6108783", "SRR6108784")

up_ids   <- res_table$gene_id[res_table$direction == "up in KO"]
down_ids <- res_table$gene_id[res_table$direction == "down in KO"]

consistent_up   <- apply(norm[up_ids, ],   1, function(x) min(x[ko]) > max(x[wt]))
consistent_down <- apply(norm[down_ids, ], 1, function(x) max(x[ko]) < min(x[wt]))

mean(consistent_up)      # fraction of "up" genes where KO > WT in every sample
mean(consistent_down)    # fraction of "down" genes where KO < WT in every sample
```


# Section 11: Volcano plot

```{r Volcano plot}
volcano_df <- res_table[!is.na(res_table$padj), ]

p_volcano <- EnhancedVolcano::EnhancedVolcano(volcano_df,
    lab      = volcano_df$label,
    x        = "log2FC_shrunk",
    y        = "padj",
    pCutoff  = padj_cutoff,
    FCcutoff = lfc_cutoff,
    selectLab = c("MIG1", head(volcano_df$label, 14)),   # MIG1 plus the 14 most significant
    drawConnectors = TRUE,
    title    = "mig1 deletion vs wild type",
    subtitle = "shrunken log2 fold change")

p_volcano
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "volcano.png"), p_volcano, width = 8, height = 7, dpi = 300)
```
